As we see, the early Church does nothing but imitate the Master. This prayer of Christ, for its part, tells us that we are before a Jesus who is always in constant search of what pleases God. Jesus shows himself as one who is acting under the impulse of the Father and at the same time in an attitude of asking for divine assistance upon the future leaders of the new people of God whom he is about to choose.

Another symptomatic episode is that of the messianic confession at Caesarea Philippi. Let us listen to the version of Lk 9:18-21: «Now it happened that as Jesus was praying alone, with only the disciples near him…». Note that Jesus prays alone; never in the Synoptics is Jesus presented praying with others. «…He asked them: «Who do the crowds say that I am?». And they answered: «John the Baptist; but others say Elijah; and others, that one of the prophets of old has risen». Then he said to them: «But who do you say that I am?». Peter answered: «The Christ of God». Here too Christ prays before prompting the messianic confession.

This confession represents, according to the Gospels, a kind of watershed in the messianic life of Jesus. One could say that everything tends toward this moment and everything unfolds from this point onward. The fact is evident above all in Mark, where the structure of the Gospel pivots on this event. Jesus, who by his way of acting stirs up questions in the crowd, in the leaders of the people, in the twelve, at a certain point takes the initiative and has the twelve say who he truly is. In the following part of the Gospel Jesus then restricts all his messianic activity to the Twelve, because by now the leaders of the people no longer listen to him, nor do the crowds follow him. From this moment onward we have a Jesus who devotes himself above all to explicit catechesis on his own messianic identity and speaks clearly about the end that awaits him. Here then are the three announcements

As for the prayer of Christ, it is evident that in this event it still appears as a prayer in search of the Father's will. Jesus seeks what the Father wants, what is pleasing to Him. Moreover, as in the preceding prayer, Jesus presents to the Father his request on behalf of the faith of the twelve, he beseeches the Father to give them the strength needed for their full adherence to the Messiah. Now it is a matter of asking for help to be able to live this faith, which before long they will have to witness to. Jesus, in fact, will put this still imperfect and embryonic faith of theirs into crisis, correcting its mistaken trajectories.

We have, finally, a text I mention briefly: Lk 22:31-32. Jesus at the Last Supper says he has prayed for Peter: «Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded to have you, that he might sift you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail; and when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers». Here too we have the same kind of prayer. Therefore those few hints of the praying Jesus or of the prayers of Jesus that we find in the Gospel of Luke concern precisely a Jesus who prays his mission, a Jesus whose prayer has as its object the Father's plan for him and who turns to the experiential book of his own mission to make it the subject of his own dialogue with the Father.

Saturday

FS pp. 147-149, «The mysticism of suffering… I loved it much and I love it greatly»

Rosa Gattorno belongs to the host of so many great lovers who, like Saint Teresa of Avila, Saint John of the Cross, Saint Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi, Saint Veronica Giuliani, made suffering, so to speak, the reason for their existence: a mission, that of completing the sufferings of Christ (cf. Col 1:24), collaborating in his redemptive immolation.

In such a mission suffering is inseparable from love: love is the cause of suffering, suffering is the expression of love. In Mother Rosa's Memoirs one passes constantly from harrowing pages, where she lays bare her sufferings of spirit - darkness, abandonments by God, temptations to despair - to others in which we see her enjoying intimate loving union with the Beloved, or experiencing the impetuous fires that force her to cry out: «Love, you make me die!». The same cry of pain-love issues from her heart when she experiences the shivers caused by the interior wounds of the hands, the feet and the side, or by the chain fixed in the flesh.

It was in the process of mystical purification, at the beginning of her widowhood, that she discovered the treasure of suffering. She recalls it beautifully, in her allegorical language, in the opening of the book Travails and Comforts:

«… My Crucified taught me to suffer and, like the honey of bees, enclosed in those precious combs, he preserved suffering for me, which turned into sweetness. From time to time he gave me some of this nectar to taste and, with sublime lessons, made me understand how so much delight was drawn from suffering, though nature rebelled against it….

My Crucified left me alone and, like the bride of the Canticles, I went wandering in that forest to seek him, taking a step forward on the path and another back. All the little branches were dry and all intertwined in the sign of crosses.

- Do you too join in my sadness? - I kept saying to them.

As I stopped, my Crucified placed his heavy cross upon my shoulders and, taking from me the terror of suffering, left me an ardent love for it. I loved it much and I love it greatly» (TC, p. 3-5).

3rd Sunday of Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 125-127, par. 2.3

Besides the ineffable encounter in the sacrament of the Eucharist (sacrifice and communion), through the sacrament of penance Jesus refines and deepens the faith that was given to us in baptism, by which God «has delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of his beloved Son» (Col 1:13).

By virtue of this sacrament we adhere to Christ and live in Him; grace has been given to us, that is, the divine life which, in order to transform us into God, requires nonetheless free and ever more responsible collaboration on our part.

With confirmation, which is the completion of baptism, we become aware that spiritual growth is the work of the Holy Spirit, who with his gifts shapes in us the image of Christ Jesus.

The Father «saved us, in virtue of his own mercy, by the washing of rebirth and renewal in the Holy Spirit, which he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ» (Tit 3:5-6).

With the sacrament of penance the «washing of rebirth» is renewed in us.

Returning from the confessional, Saint Catherine of Siena, doctor of the Church, would exclaim: «I have gone to wash my soul in the Blood of Christ».

This is how it truly happens in every encounter with Christ in the sacrament of mercy.

The daughters of Saint Anne and all the members of the Family of the mother of the Immaculate live in the sacrifice of Christ, who never ceases to intercede with the Father on our behalf: «For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest: holy, innocent, unstained, separated from sinners, exalted above the heavens; he has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for his own sins and then for those of the people, since he did this once for all when he offered up himself» (Heb 7:26-27).

Closely united to the unceasing prayer of Jesus for us and with us is the prayer of the mother of God, Mary most holy, who for us offers the most sacred heart of Jesus, his perfect adorations, his unspeakable love, his eminent holiness, to the adorable Trinity, for its greater glory, for the salvation of the world, and the liberation of the souls in Purgatory, always imploring from Jesus pardon for the many offenses done to God, especially in our time. It is She who, while she helps us to advance each day on the way of virtue and perfection, turns away from us the chastisements of God.

The gaze of God resting upon Her who is Immaculate and refuge of sinners always finds in her every delight and every pleasure.

Humanity, in the luminous transparency of Mary most holy, finds in her intercession and defense.

Monday

D. pp. 76-78, par. 4

The enemy's challenge does not weaken her fidelity to the will of the Father and her sole yearning to be like Jesus and in Jesus. In her words one feels all the strength that the life-witness of the Beloved brings her: «…

obedient unto death, even death on a cross» (Phil 2:8); «…Jesus said: It is finished. And bowing his head he gave up his spirit…» (Jn 19:30).

If Jesus died for the life of the Church and of the world, she too is ready to die for the life of the Work of God:

«All at once I feel someone approaching. Oh! it was my Good Jesus, my Beloved! I felt myself clasped to Him and remained thus absorbed in my Good. I saw a man who held a stylus in his hand, in the act of wanting to plunge it into my throat… with an angry voice he said to me: «withdraw from this work or I will kill you»…».

«It will never be. Even if I had to undergo all the martyrdoms of this earth I will always be your slave and you my Beloved.

A Voice answered me: look at me, how gentle I am, and a little lamb appeared to me. It had a wound in its breast that poured forth blood: what an impression this sight made on me! It caressed me, its nearness made me die of love. The fire on the side of the heart was very strong and lasted quite a while, alas. My Love, I am dying. Oh my dear little Lamb!» (M. 1.1, pp. 147-148).

United with her Beloved she frequently lives the obligatory passage of trial, but those of the absence of the Beloved are atrocious.

When the Beloved is present, even if not yet in fullness as in glory, paradise is in her; but she must pass through the sorrowful experience of Him who lived in infinite measure this void between presence and absence, with that density which those who reject the divine presence are destined to live.

This void, willed and not removed, is the permanent sorrow of the Beloved and she must taste it in order to offer herself in the name of those who inflict it on him, so that they may arrive at an adequate knowledge of the reality of God and of man.

The personal, deep experience of what the Beloved makes her live transforms her too, and she becomes the Beloved. Only so can he ask her to unite herself to his redemptive offering for the salvation of sinners:

«Jesus said to me thus: «See, my beloved, when you rejected me and fled my sight, so the cloud in which I was, and I called you many times and you always turned elsewhere and drove me away, and I abandoned you, you sought me, but could find me no more. So it is with the damned, they will find me no more!». Oh! what sufferings, yes my Good, it is a cruel anguish that I felt. Oh! the mere thought of it makes me shudder…» (M. 1.1, p. 168).

This infused knowledge motivates, beyond every human criterion, her absolute offering for the salvation of sinners.

Tuesday

TC pp. 323-325, «She returns with the fine ship… to be incorporated into his Church»

She returns with the fine ship flying the flag: SUFFERING - LOVE, to incorporate it into the Roman Church.

With all the strength I had, I ran to take the little boat to carry it to where the Vicar is; but a stormy sea rises, a contrary wind dashes me against a rock. The weeping and the prayers were beyond compare. I had almost lost hope of being able to put it back to sea; so damaged by that blow, surely, on any sea it fills with water. I wept much, but I was sure that my Master would give me another, or else make this one beautiful. Each of those on the ships said his own piece, and one was so pressing that I do not know what he would have done to me.

After a great struggle, my little ship came out far more beautiful, and it was elegant: it had its gilded rudder, a most beautiful compass; no longer the ragged sail, but an elegant flag that bore the inscription: Suffering and Love!

To two dear creatures, who joined me, I gave an oar apiece, and I was busy getting straight into port and then (carrying myself) to the feet of the great Vicar. What a surprise for the commanders of the big ships! They did not speak at all, but full of wonder they looked at me.

One, who could not restrain himself, comes close and wants to know how it had happened, and tells me to take care not to do this or that anymore. I turned to him:

- I beg you to leave me, because your argument is hardly logical: in the Work of the Lord philosophy, theology, calculation have no place; all empty chairs!

- What kind of reasoning is this? - he said to me.

- Poor slave that I am, I never studied and understand nothing: one thing only have I tried to study and to perfect myself in this subject: the will of God! to try to do it blindly, in perfect abandonment to Him, like a faithful slave to her beloved Master.

He looks at me and then, with a gesture of contempt:

- She is a fanatic! She has little judgment: let her go! And he addresses words to my workers to seduce them, but they, in an imperious tone, answer him to withdraw, that he has nothing to do with them.

He had guessed exactly what he said of me: a slave who knows nothing, truly uneducated in the sciences:

- And it is for this that Jesus took you to work you in his own way, so that no one can say this is the work of man, but only divine wisdom has cooperated - my voice said thus.

Brought, together with my two companions, to the feet of Peter, the great apostle, I knew nothing else to tell him except that he should say many things for me to my God: that I was bringing the little boat to the feet of his Vicar, so that it might be incorporated into his Church.
